items.title: How Social Media Weaponized Your Insecurities
items.summary: In episode 1013 of the SuperDataScience Podcast, Jon Krohn talks with Dr. Cathy O'Neil, NY Times Bestselling Author about her book "The Shame Machine." She explains how social media companies have developed a 'tricky' method of shame profiteering, designing platforms that encourage users to shame each other, making it addictive and exploitative. Dr. O'Neil also introduces her framework for valid shame, based on 'voice and choice,' and expresses concern about AI chatbots as a false refuge from social media's harmful dynamics.

items.title: How AI Agents Should Use Memory and Retrieval
items.summary:
For AI agents, memory is not the same thing as knowledge retrieval—and context is not infinite.

In this Short, Micheal Lanham, author of AI Agents in Action, Second Edition, explains how memory, retrieval, and context management should work together so agents can use the right information at the right time without becoming noisy, expensive, or unreliable.

Learn more about the book: https://hubs.la/Q04p-7WX0

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Tech Mahindra's CIO Says LLMs Are Already Obsolete
items.summary:
Nikhil Malhotra believes the industry should stop calling them large language models entirely, because language prediction is a solved problem and the real frontier is action. 

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Nikhil Malhotra, Chief Innovation Officer and Global Head of AI & Emerging Technologies at Tech Mahindra, to break down why the world needs to shift from large language models to large action models, how domain-specific language action models could end agent sprawl in enterprise AI, why symbolic reasoning borrowed from neuroscience may matter more than adding compute, and why India's biggest AI opportunity lies in diffusion and fundamental research rather than chasing bigger foundation models.

items.title: Course Preview: Introduction to Partial Differential Equations
items.summary:
Dive into partial differential equations with Introduction to Partial Differential Equations from Wolfram kernel developer and professor Aram Manaselyan. Learn first- and second-order PDEs, including the heat, wave and Laplace equations, plus four famous modern PDEs—Black–Scholes, Schrödinger, Maxwell and Navier–Stokes. Built-in Wolfram Language functions handle everything from solving PDEs to computing eigenvalues and eigenfunctions, with interactive visualizations to build physical intuition.

Enroll at https://wolfr.am/Partial-Diff-Eq for video lessons, exercises, quizzes, a scratch notebook and the Wolfram AI Course Assistant to help along the way.

#PDE #WolframLanguage #WolframU #Mathematica #appliedmath #mathematics #appliedmaths

items.title: Course Preview: Introduction to Laplace Transforms
items.summary:
Master Laplace transforms with this course from longtime math educator Juan Ariel Ortiz Navarro, covering the integral definition, elementary properties, inverse transforms, numerical approximations and complex inversion. A final section applies these techniques to ordinary and partial differential equations, fractional calculus, sums and integrals—all with Wolfram Language's built-in functions and visualization tools to help you understand your solutions.

Visit https://wolfr.am/Laplace-Transforms for video lessons, exercises, quizzes, a scratch notebook and the Wolfram AI Course Assistant to help along the way.  Earn a course completion certificate or a Wolfram Level 1 certification by passing the final exam.

#LaplaceTransform #WolframLanguage #WolframU #Mathematica #AppliedMath #Mathematics #DifferentialEquations #Calculus #WolframU

items.title: Course Preview: Introduction to Multivariable Calculus
items.summary:
Extend your calculus skills into two and three dimensions in Multivariable Calculus, from math professor and Wolfram visualization developer Tim McDevitt. Essential for engineering, economics, physics, statistics and data science, this course pairs symbolic and numerical calculations with rich plotting so you can solve problems multiple ways and see the results. Builds on single-variable calculus, with a Level 1 certification available at the end.

Enroll at https://wolfr.am/Multivar-Calculus for video lessons, exercises, quizzes, a scratch notebook and the Wolfram AI Course Assistant to help along the way.

#MultivariableCalculus #WolframLanguage #WolframU #Mathematica #LearnMath

items.title: Course Preview: Introduction to Discrete Mathematics
items.summary:
Explore the world of integers with this intuitive introduction to discrete mathematics, created by Wolfram kernel developer Marc Vicuna. Ideal for computer science and software engineering, this course uses Wolfram Language to model information, build efficient algorithms and solve real problems—no advanced math background required, just curiosity.

Check out https://wolfr.am/Discrete-Math for video lessons, exercises, quizzes, a scratch notebook, and the AI Assistant to help along the way.

 New to Wolfram Language? Start with the Elementary Introduction course first; want more? Check out Discrete Calculus or Cryptography next.

items.title: Course Preview: Introduction to Complex Analysis
items.summary:
Explore complex analysis, a cornerstone of mathematics with real applications in physics and engineering. Taught by Wolfram Research developer Marco Saragnese, this course covers elementary functions, the Cauchy–Riemann equations, complex integration, Cauchy's theorem and the residue theorem—using Wolfram Language's visualization and computation tools to skip tedious calculation and focus on the concepts that matter.

Sign up free at https://wolfr.am/Complex-Analysis for video lessons, exercises, quizzes, a scratch notebook and the Wolfram AI Course Assistant to help along the way. 

Recommended prerequisites: Introduction to Calculus and Multivariable Calculus, both available free on Wolfram U.
https://wolfr.am/Intro-to-Calculus
https://wolfr.am/Multivar-Calculus

items.title: Course Preview: An Elementary Introduction to the Wolfram Language
items.summary:
Start learning Wolfram Language from the ground up with this course based on Stephen Wolfram's book An Elementary Introduction to the Wolfram Language, taught by longtime language developer David Withoff. Beginning with simple examples like basic arithmetic and plots, the lessons build up to real-world applications—interactive sliders and buttons, geographic and chemistry data, web-deployed apps, graphics and video processing.

Go to https://wolfr.am/EIWL-Course for video lessons, exercises, quizzes, a scratch notebook and the Wolfram AI Course Assistant to help along the way. 

#WolframLanguage #wolfram  #CodingForBeginners #LearnToCode

Calculus is the science of how things change—and Introduction to Calculus, taught by Wolfram mathematician Devendra Kapadia, uses Wolfram Language's powerful built-in functions to make limits, derivatives and integrals click. Beyond calculation, you'll build plots and animations to visualize concepts, backed by video lessons, exercises, quizzes, problem sessions and practice exams.

Check out  https://wolfr.am/Intro-to-Calculus for the full interactive course and the Wolfram AI Course Assistant to help along the way. 

Examples are from the Wolfram eTextbook Series https://www.wolfram-media.com/series/etextbooks/
